lines: **Chunking: 600 characters, 20% overlap** (run R5). Among the chunking runs it scored the highest overall (1.00), with retrieval MRR 1.00. Smaller chunks give more precise passages, but a policy rule and its condition can be split across chunks. Larger chunks keep rules together, but they put more unrelated text into the prompt (total tokens per run: R1=8310, R2=6404, R3=10873, R4=8338, R5=8261).

**Embeddings: Open-source BGE-small.** In the end-to-end runs, OpenAI scored 0.99 and BGE 1.00. Across all 9 chunking configurations, average retrieval was: OpenAI recall@4 1.00 / MRR 0.97, against BGE 1.00 / 1.00. OpenAI costs $0.02 per 1M tokens ($0.000054 for this corpus) and takes about 275 ms per query over the network. BGE is free, runs locally in about 17 ms per query, and keeps policy text inside the company. Since quality is essentially equal, the free and private model wins.

**Prompt: P1 (concise).** P1 averaged 42 output tokens with overall 0.99, and P2 averaged 92 tokens with overall 0.91 (citation 0.95 vs 0.85). P2's evidence bullets make answers easier to audit, but they did not improve accuracy enough to justify the longer output. P1 stays the default, and P2 is useful when an auditor needs to see the evidence.
